detail.body:
## Motivation

Block-FP8 checkpoints (128x128 weight scales, e.g. Qwen3-32B-FP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8) run their linears on XPU in two steps. First `per_token_group_quant_fp8` quantizes the activation. Then `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` calls `scaled_mm` (oneDNN).

At decode sizes that path streams the fp8 weight at only 175-350 GB/s on Arc Pro B70; the bf16 GEMM reaches 510-590 GB/s. So Qwen3-32B-FP8 decodes no faster than bf16, even though it reads half the bytes. Xe2 has no FP8 math, so fp8 activations buy nothing. The win is bandwidth: keep the activation in bf16 and stream the fp8 weight once.

## Dependency

The fused GEMM is `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20`, added in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#587. sglang currently pins sgl-kernel-xpu 0.5.0, which does not have it.

- This PR detects the op (`has_xpu_w8a16_gemm`). Without it, block-FP8 linears keep today's `scaled_mm` path unchanged, so this PR is safe to merge before the kernel release.
- The speedup arrives with the sgl-kernel-xpu version bump that includes #587.
- Until then, the fused-path unit test skips in CI and the dequant test runs.

## Modifications

- New `kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_w8a16_xpu.py`, with `xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear(input, weight, weight_scale, bias)`:
  - Up to 512 rows it calls `fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20`, which dequantizes in registers and streams the weight once.
  - Above 512 rows the GEMM is compute-bound. The weight is dequantized to bf16 by a small Triton kernel (one program per 128x128 scale block, edge blocks masked) and multiplied with `F.linear`. On these shapes that is faster than both `scaled_mm` and the fused kernel.
  - 512 is where the two paths tie at Qwen3-32B TP4 shapes on B70; the comment says so.
- `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`: on XPU, `_dispatch_auto_backend` returns `xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` when the op exists. That function falls back to `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` when there is a static input scale, when the input is not bf16, or when the block size is not `[128, 128]`.
- The fused path asserts a row-contiguous `weight` and a k-contiguous `weight_scale`, the only layouts sgl-kernel-xpu#587 was validated on. The dequant kernel reads `weight_scale` through both of its strides, so it is correct for either scale layout.
- New `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_fp8_w8a16_xpu.py`:
  - The dequant kernel must be bit-exact against a reference, including partial scale blocks (N=320, K=448).
  - Both paths (1, 24, 512 and 513 rows, with bias) must match the dequantized-weight reference.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K: sgl-eval, full 1319 questions, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8, thinking off, max 2048 tokens, seed 0.

| model | old FP8 path | this PR | bf16 checkpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-32B-FP8, TP4 | 94.84% | 95.22% | 94.31-94.77% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP2 | 95.00% | 94.77% | - |

`test_fp8_w8a16_xpu.py`: 2 passed on Arc Pro B70 with the #587 op loaded; on the pinned sgl-kernel-xpu 0.5.0 the fused-op case skips.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:**
- Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, compute-runtime 26.31.
- The op from sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#587 was loaded as a torch library fragment on top of the released wheel.
- Server flags: cookbook BMG flags plus `--attention-backend intel_xpu --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`.

Per GEMM at decode (M=1, cold weights, in an XPU graph), Qwen3-32B TP4 shapes:

| GEMM | old `scaled_mm` path | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| qkv (N=2560, K=5120) | 49.7 us | 28.5 us (460 GB/s) |
| o_proj (N=5120, K=2048) | 38.4 | 21.7 (482 GB/s) |
| gate_up (N=12800, K=5120) | 222.6 | 119.2 (550 GB/s) |
| down (N=5120, K=6400) | 113.4 | 61.7 (531 GB/s) |
| per layer | 424 | 231 (1.84x) |

Prefill, one layer of 4 linears, in an XPU graph:

| rows | bf16 checkpoint | old `scaled_mm` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 547 us | 774 | 545 (fused) |
| 512 | 926 | 1943 | 1973 (fused) |
| 2048 | 3432 | 8295 | 4410 (dequant + bf16) |
| 4096 | 6783 | 16952 | 7975 (dequant + bf16) |

Prefill stays slower than the bf16 checkpoint, because the weight is still dequantized or streamed as fp8. It is much faster than the old path, though: c=16 TTFT for Qwen3-32B is 1049 ms, against 935 ms for bf16 and 1669 ms for the old FP8 path.

End to end, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 256 out:

| Qwen3-32B, TP4 | c=1 TPOT | c=4 | c=16 | c=32 | c=16 tok/s | c=32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 checkpoint | 31.57 ms | 32.48 | 34.97 | 40.28 | 415 | 715 |
| FP8, old path | 30.98 | 31.80 | 35.23 | 40.91 | 384 | 653 |
| FP8, this PR | **19.88** | 20.98 | 23.78 | 29.58 | **575** | **926** |

| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP2 (attention linears) | c=1 TPOT | c=4 | c=16 | c=32 | c=32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old path | 8.95 ms | 13.65 | 22.70 | 29.82 | 1010 |
| this PR | **7.34** | 11.93 | 21.08 | 28.18 | 1070 |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 does not load at TP4: the per-rank MoE intermediate size, 768/4 = 192, is not a multiple of the 128 block. TP2 works.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+"""Weight-only block-FP8 linear (W8A16) for Intel Xe2 GPUs.
+
+Decode-sized inputs run sgl-kernel-xpu's fused dequant GEMM, which streams the fp8 weight once.
+Larger inputs are compute-bound, so they dequantize the weight to bf16 and use the bf16 GEMM.
+"""
+
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+# Measured on Arc Pro B70 at Qwen3-32B TP4 shapes: the two paths tie at 512 rows, and above
+# that the weight dequant plus bf16 GEMM wins.
+_FUSED_MAX_ROWS = 512
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def has_xpu_w8a16_gemm() -> bool:
+    try:
+        import sgl_kernel  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return hasattr(torch.ops.sgl_kernel, "fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20")
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dequant_block_fp8_kernel(
+    w_ptr,
+    s_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    N,
+    K,
+    stride_wn,
+    stride_sn,
+    stride_sk,
+    stride_on,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid_n = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_k = tl.program_id(1)
+    offs_n = pid_n * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    offs_k = pid_k * BLOCK_K + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    mask = (offs_n[:, None] < N) & (offs_k[None, :] < K)
+    w = tl.load(
+        w_ptr + offs_n[:, None] * stride_wn + offs_k[None, :], mask=mask, other=0.0
+    )
+    # One program covers exactly one 128x128 scale block.
+    s = tl.load(s_ptr + pid_n * stride_sn + pid_k * stride_sk)
+    out = (w.to(tl.float32) * s).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offs_n[:, None] * stride_on + offs_k[None, :], out, mask=mask)
+
+
+def dequant_block_fp8_weight(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, weight_scale: torch.Tensor, dtype: torch.dtype
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """fp8 e4m3 [N, K] with fp32 [ceil(N / 128), ceil(K / 128)] block scales -> dtype [N, K]."""
+    n, k = weight.shape
+    out = torch.empty((n, k), dtype=dtype, device=weight.device)
+    grid = (triton.cdiv(n, 128), triton.cdiv(k, 128))
+    _dequant_block_fp8_kernel[grid](
+        weight,
+        weight_scale,
+        out,
+        n,
+        k,
+        weight.stride(0),
+        weight_scale.stride(0),
+        weight_scale.stride(1),
+        out.stride(0),
+        BLOCK_N=128,
+        BLOCK_K=128,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear(
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """bf16 input [..., K] @ (fp8 e4m3 weight [N, K] * fp32 [N / 128, K / 128] scales)^T."""
+    input_2d = input.reshape(-1, input.shape[-1])
+    if input_2d.shape[0] > _FUSED_MAX_ROWS:
+        weight_bf16 = dequant_block_fp8_weight(weight, weight_scale, input.dtype)
+        output = torch.nn.functional.linear(input_2d, weight_bf16, bias)
+    else:
+        if input_2d.stride(-1) != 1:
+            input_2d = input_2d.contiguous()
+        # The fused op's layout contract is external; fail loudly rather than
+        # feed it a layout sgl-kernel-xpu#587 was not validated against.
+        assert weight.stride(-1) == 1, (
+            "fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20 requires row-contiguous weight"
+        )
+        assert weight_scale.stride(1) == 1, (
+            "fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20 requires k-contiguous weight_scale "
+            "(prepare_xpu_block_scale_for_scaled_mm's transposed layout is unsupported)"
+        )
+        output = torch.empty(
+            (input_2d.shape[0], weight.shape[0]),
+            dtype=input.dtype,
+            device=input.device,
+        )
+        torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20(output, input_2d, weight, weight_scale)
+        if bias is not None:
+            output += bias
+    return output.view(*input.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0])

+"""Block-FP8 W8A16 linear on XPU must match the dequantized-weight reference on both of its paths.
+
+Inputs up to 512 rows run sgl_kernel's fused W8A16 GEMM; larger inputs dequantize the weight with a
+Triton kernel that maps one program to one 128x128 scale block, including partial edge blocks.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+
+def _make_weight(n: int, k: int):
+    weight = (torch.randn(n, k, device="xpu") * 64).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.rand(-(n // -128), -(k // -128), device="xpu") * 1e-2 + 1e-3
+    dense = (
+        weight.float()
+        * scale.repeat_interleave(128, 0)[:n].repeat_interleave(128, 1)[:, :k]
+    )
+    return weight, scale, dense
+
+
+class TestFp8W8A16LinearXPU(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        if not torch.xpu.is_available():
+            self.skipTest("XPU not available")
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+
+    def test_dequant_handles_partial_scale_blocks(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.fp8_w8a16_xpu import dequant_block_fp8_weight
+
+        weight, scale, dense = _make_weight(n=320, k=448)
+        out = dequant_block_fp8_weight(weight, scale, torch.bfloat16)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, dense.to(torch.bfloat16), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+    def test_fused_and_dequant_paths_match_reference(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.fp8_w8a16_xpu import (
+            has_xpu_w8a16_gemm,
+            xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear,
+        )
+
+        if not has_xpu_w8a16_gemm():
+            self.skipTest("sgl_kernel lacks fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20")
+        weight, scale, dense = _make_weight(n=2560, k=5120)
+        bias = torch.randn(2560, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for rows in (1, 24, 512, 513):
+            x = torch.randn(rows, 5120, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            out = xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear(
+                input=x.view(1, rows, 5120),
+                weight=weight,
+                weight_scale=scale,
+                bias=bias,
+            )
+            ref = x.float() @ dense.t() + bias.float()
+            self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, rows, 2560))
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                out.view(rows, 2560).float(),
+                ref,
+                rtol=1e-2,
+                atol=1e-2 * ref.abs().max().item(),
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
